record.context_brief: Zero distributions of Wright and hypergeometric functions
record.original_question:
For Wright functions pΨ_q and generalized hypergeometric functions
pF_q that are entire, obtain information about the
distribution of their zeros.

evidence.quote: Problem 27 ([24], p. 90 in [51]). The Wright function (or Fox-Wright function) is defined as ∞ Qp X Γ(aj k + bj ) xk Qj=1 , (2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $p,q$ and parameters $a_1,\dots,a_p, b_1,\dots,b_q \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a_j>0$ (and suitable conditions ensuring convergence everywhere), define the Wright (Fox–Wright) function by
$$
{}_p\Psi_q\!\left[\begin{array}{c}(a_1,b_1),\dots,(a_p,b_p)\\ (c_1,d_1),\dots,(c_q,d_q)\end{array};x\right] \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{\prod_{j=1}^{p}\Gamma(a_j k + b_j)}{\prod_{j=1}^{q}\Gamma(c_j k + d_j)}\,\frac{x^{k}}{k!},
$$
and the generalized hypergeometric function by
$$
{}_pF_q\!\left[\begin{array}{c}\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_p\\ \beta_1,\dots,\beta_q\end{array};x\right] \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(\alpha_1)_k\cdots(\alpha_p)_k}{(\beta_1)_k\cdots(\beta_q)_k}\,\frac{x^{k}}{k!},
$$
where $(\alpha)_k = \Gamma(\alpha+k)/\Gamma(\alpha)$ is the Pochhammer symbol. Assume that the parameters are chosen so that ${}_p\Psi_q$ and ${}_pF_q$ are entire functions of $x \in \mathbb{C}$.

Determine the distribution of the zeros (in $\mathbb{C}$) of such entire Wright functions ${}_p\Psi_q$ and entire generalized hypergeometric functions ${}_pF_q$: specifically, locate the zeros (e.g., conditions under which all zeros are real, or lie on a particular ray such as the negative real axis), describe their asymptotic distribution and density, determine the order and type of these entire functions as zero-distribution invariants, and characterize the parameter ranges for which the zeros possess prescribed reality, simplicity, or interlacing properties.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: for the classical Wright function φ(ρ, β; z) with ρ > 0, all sufficiently large zeros are simple and lie on the negative real axis; for −1/3 ≤ ρ < 0 they lie on the positive real axis. Specific conjectures (e.g., that certain Fox–Wright functions f_m have only negative real zeros) remain open, and a complete characterization of zero distributions for general entire ${}_p\Psi_q$ and ${}_pF_q$ has not been obtained.

status_evidence.title: Fox–Wright function - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Fox–Wright function is a generalisation of the generalised hypergeometric function pFq(z) based on ideas of Charles Fox (1928) and E. Maitland Wright (1935).
status_evidence.claim: Defines the Fox–Wright function generalizing pFq.

status_evidence.title: Zero distribution of Wright function (survey results)
status_evidence.snippet: In the case ρ > 0 all zeros with large enough k are simple and are lying on the negative real semi-axis. In the case −1/3 ≤ ρ < 0 all zeros with large enough k are simple, lying on the positive real semi-axis.
status_evidence.claim: Partial zero-location results for Wright function are known.

status_evidence.title: On the generalized Wright function
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 3.17: for each positive integer m, the Fox–Wright function f_m(x) has only real negative zeros.
status_evidence.claim: Specific conjectures on real zeros remain open.
